blogs.title: When Antibody Logic Goes Rogue: Autoimmune HIT and the Pitfalls of Conventional SRA Interpretation
blogs.description: A deep dive into how the classic serotonin‑release assay can mask a true autoimmune HIT (aHIT) when antibodies exhibit heparin‑independent activation. We’ll explore the unique laboratory signature seen in this case—serotonin release at 0 U/mL, partial Fc‑receptor blockade—and what it means for daily practice when the ‘indeterminate’ SRA masks a potentially catastrophic bleed‑risk scenario.

blogs.title: Early Post‑Cardiac Surgery Thrombocytopenia: Beyond the Traditional 5‑10 Day Window
blogs.description: We unpack how pre‑operative heparin exposure can accelerate HIT onset to POD5 and earlier. Strategies for anticipation, early recognition and differential diagnosis in the elderly after CPB, and how to integrate pre‑operative anticoagulation history into the postoperative work‑up.

blogs.title: Managing a Thrombotic Storm: Choosing Non‑Heparin Anticoagulation in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: A guide to anticoagulation in aHIT—from initial argatroban in the setting of a recent stroke to the eventual switch to fondaparinux. We’ll compare direct thrombin inhibitors, indirect factor Xa inhibitors and the off‑label use of fondaparinux, discuss antithrombin dosing and when to consider intravenous immunoglobulin to blunt hypercoagulability.

blogs.title: Hypercoagulability in the ICU: Untangling Fibrinogen, D‑Dimer, and Schistocytosis in HIT
blogs.description: How rising d‑dimer, falling fibrinogen, and peripheral schistocytes can signal a consumptive coagulopathy in aHIT. We’ll review how to interpret these lab trends, their prognostic value, and the timing of therapeutic interventions to mitigate organ‑level damage.

blogs.title: From Platelet Drop to Stroke: The Clinical Spectrum of Autoimmune HIT Post‑Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: We explore the clinical framework of aHIT: profound thrombocytopenia, early onset, thrombotic complications, and impaired response to IgG‑depletion therapies. Practical tips for clinicians to recognize the red flags, avoid misattributing thrombocytopenia to transfusion or infection, and chart a clear path to recovery.
